Definition: a boiler or basket; also the mandrake (as an aphrodisiac)
KeyPassages: Genesis 30:14; Jeremiah 24:1; Song of Solomon 7:13; Genesis 30:15
BiblicalUsage: Mandrakes, and baskets, the love-apples Reuben found in the field at wheat harvest, which Rachel begged from Leah, and the Song says the mandrakes give a sweet smell at our gates. The same root names the baskets of figs Jeremiah saw set before the temple, one good and one evil.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mandrakes tell the truth about grasping for what only God can give: Rachel traded a night for a plant, and the plant could not open her womb. God gives children; the field only gives apples.
